description: Add the strongly typed DocumentCache configuration contract bound from DataManagement:DocumentCache. Model Targets, ReadAcceleration, and Projector settings with the story-owned defaults, use the built-in .NET TimeSpan binder for durations, and implement validation for positive durations and numeric settings. Model a normalized immutable target key with the same case-insensitive tenant-key comparison semantics as IDataStoreProvider, positive DataStoreId enforcement, empty-string default tenant support, tenant whitespace rejection, configured-spelling preservation only for sanitized diagnostics, and duplicate detection after normalization. Keep an empty Targets array valid even when read acceleration is enabled, and do not add compatibility aliases for legacy scan, audit, source-poll, scan-age-readiness, or exact-count backlog settings.
acceptance-criteria: DocumentCacheOptions binds from DataManagement:DocumentCache and defaults Targets to empty, ReadAcceleration.Enabled to false, Projector.PollInterval to 00:00:05, Projector.PageSize to 100, Projector.MaxConcurrentTargets to 2, Projector.FailureBackoff to 00:00:30, Projector.BaselineHighWaterMark to 1000, and ReadAcceleration.DirectFillTimeout to 00:00:00.250.

Validation fails startup for nonpositive PollInterval, PageSize, MaxConcurrentTargets, FailureBackoff, BaselineHighWaterMark, DirectFillTimeout, nonpositive DataStoreId, tenant keys with leading or trailing whitespace, and duplicate targets after tenant normalization.
An empty Targets array is valid and selects no projection or cache-use target, regardless of the read-acceleration gate.
Legacy DocumentCache scan, audit, source-poll, scan-age-readiness, and exact-count backlog setting names are not consumed as aliases for the new options.

Unit tests cover defaults, TimeSpan binding, duplicate target normalization, default tenant representation, empty targets, invalid numeric values, tenant whitespace rejection, and legacy setting non-consumption.

description: Register DocumentCacheOptions through the existing options-validation pattern and publish supported appsettings examples. Add startup diagnostics that report the effective default/tuned settings and target count without exposing raw tenant display names, connection strings, credentials, host names, database names, or other physical identifiers. Keep membership restart-bound by using IOptions at startup instead of IOptionsMonitor, file-watch reload, route qualifiers, JWT data-store claims, recent requests, or CMS inventory enumeration.
acceptance-criteria: DocumentCacheOptions is registered with validation-on-start in the DMS service setup alongside the existing options validators.
Startup diagnostics include the effective projector/read-acceleration settings and sanitized configured target identifiers, and they omit connection strings and physical source details.

Supported appsettings examples include the DataManagement:DocumentCache shape, the implementation defaults, and links or comments pointing operators to the authoritative design document rather than duplicating behavioral prose.
The registered configuration path does not use IOptionsMonitor or any runtime file-watch mechanism for target membership.
Tests or service-registration assertions prove malformed DocumentCache options fail during application startup validation.

description: Extend the DMS data-store metadata path so resolved Configuration Service data stores can expose an explicit normalized relational provider token. Update the DataStore record, ConfigurationServiceDataStoreProvider response mapping, fakes, and tests to carry a provider token with allowed values postgresql and sqlserver. Do not infer the token from AppSettings:Datastore and do not map CMS DataStoreType to a relational provider. Missing, blank, or unknown provider metadata must remain taskable as a resolved-but-projection/cache-ineligible diagnostic for the target resolver.
acceptance-criteria: DataStore metadata can carry a normalized relational provider token independent of DataStoreType.
ConfigurationServiceDataStoreProvider reads the explicit provider metadata when present and preserves existing decryption, route-context, tenant, caching, and logging behavior.
Provider-token normalization accepts only postgresql and sqlserver values, with missing or unknown values left distinguishable for target eligibility diagnostics.
Existing request-routing and health-check connection-string behavior remains compatible with DataStore records that lack provider metadata until DocumentCache target resolution consumes it.
Unit tests cover provider metadata present, missing, unknown, and changed across refresh responses.

description: Define the internal DocumentCache target contract types shared by the resolver, provider adapters, command classifiers, and later E18 stories. Include immutable target key, resolution state, eligibility state, effective settings, target-context generation, provider token, opaque physical-source fingerprint, lifecycle/latch observation, inventory validation result, enqueue-trigger validation result, SQL Server prerequisite details, retry/failure diagnostics, and sanitized diagnostic categories. Keep these models observational: they must not decide projection health, perform lifecycle mutations, or depend on the current HTTP request's IDataStoreSelection.
acceptance-criteria: Target contract models can represent configured, unresolved, resolved-eligible, resolved-ineligible, and replaced-generation observations for every configured target.
Lifecycle states include Disabled, Resetting, Rebuilding, and Tracking, with CacheAheadRecoveryRequired represented independently.
Provider prerequisite result models distinguish Satisfied, Disabled, Unreadable, and NotApplicable where appropriate.

Diagnostic models include target key, resolution state, provider token, generation, opaque fingerprint when available, lifecycle/latch when available, inventory/prerequisite observations, retry state, and sanitized category/message.
The contract layer exposes no raw connection string, credential, tenant display name, host, database name, or document body field.

description: Implement the physical-source fingerprint contract for resolved target execution contexts. Add provider-neutral services and provider-specific readers that read the singleton dms.DataStoreIdentity.SourceIdentity through the target connection, reject missing, malformed, or all-zero source identities as inventory failures, and compute the opaque sha256 fingerprint using the design-owned payload algorithm. The service must use the normalized relational provider token only after it matches the process provider and must not log or include raw source UUIDs outside controlled test assertions.
acceptance-criteria: The fingerprint algorithm uses UTF-8 bytes for ed-fi-dms-source-v1, NUL, provider token, NUL, and the lowercase UUID D-format source identity, and returns sha256: plus lowercase hex.
Conformance tests match the postgresql and sqlserver fingerprints for source identity f81d4fae-7dec-11d0-a765-00a0c91e6bf6 from the design.
Provider readers classify missing DataStoreIdentity, missing row, malformed UUID, all-zero UUID, and unreadable identity as inventory failures for that target only.
Fingerprint diagnostics expose only the opaque fingerprint when available and sanitized failure categories/messages otherwise.
The implementation does not compare the current fingerprint to previous observations or any CDC binding record.

description: Add PostgreSQL and SQL Server provider adapters that validate the exact 18-00/data-model DocumentCache physical inventory required for projection/cache eligibility. Validate dms.DataStoreIdentity, dms.DocumentCacheState, dms.DocumentCache, dms.DocumentProjectionWork, required singleton rows, required columns, key order, constraints, indexes, FK/cascade behavior, lifecycle constraint, and the enabled enqueue trigger/function inventory. This story reads and classifies inventory only; it must not repair, provision, migrate, reconcile schema drift, or accept renamed hand-built equivalents.
acceptance-criteria: Inventory validators assert exact stable table, constraint, index, trigger, and PostgreSQL function names from the generated 18-00 contract.
Semantic checks supplement exact-name checks so correctly named but structurally wrong objects are rejected.
Inventory failures are target-scoped and do not prevent unrelated configured targets or ordinary canonical API routing from being observed normally.
A resolved target with invalid inventory remains projection/cache-ineligible for that target-context generation.
Provider integration tests cover valid inventory, missing objects, renamed objects, disabled/missing enqueue artifacts, missing singleton rows, wrong lifecycle constraint, and peer-target isolation.

description: Add SQL Server prerequisite validation for DocumentCache target execution contexts and activation preflight inputs. Validate READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT for the target database and server-level nested triggers with sys.configurations.value_in_use = 1. Classify each prerequisite separately as satisfied, disabled, unreadable, or not applicable as appropriate. DMS must never change either setting. PostgreSQL targets should report not-applicable prerequisite details rather than silently omitting the prerequisite observation.
acceptance-criteria: SQL Server target-context initialization validates RCSI and nested triggers and records separate prerequisite observations.
A disabled or unreadable SQL Server prerequisite leaves only that target projection/cache-ineligible and emits sanitized diagnostics without changing provider settings.
An initialization-time prerequisite failure observed with lifecycle Disabled is classified as recoverable by correction and DMS/projector restart.
The same initialization-time prerequisite failure observed with Tracking, Rebuilding, or Resetting is classified as an UnsupportedIncident distinct from ordinary retryable target failure.
Activation-preflight prerequisite validation is modeled as command-local input and does not reuse a prior successful startup validation as proof.

description: Implement the process-local target execution context builder. It must resolve a configured target to data-store metadata, require a nonblank connection string, require a normalized provider token that matches AppSettings:Datastore, build provider-appropriate connection factory information without depending on request-scoped IDataStoreSelection, read the physical-source fingerprint, observe lifecycle/latch state, run inventory and provider-prerequisite validation, attach effective DocumentCache settings, and assign the target-context generation. Missing connection strings, missing/unknown provider metadata, provider mismatch, fingerprint failures, inventory failures, lifecycle failures, and prerequisite failures must produce resolved-but-ineligible target diagnostics without failing unrelated targets.
acceptance-criteria: Execution contexts are process-local and independent from the current HTTP request's IDataStoreSelection.
A resolved target with a blank connection string is projection/cache-ineligible with sanitized diagnostics.
A resolved target with missing or unknown provider metadata is projection/cache-ineligible with a provider-metadata diagnostic.
A resolved target with provider metadata that differs from AppSettings:Datastore is projection/cache-ineligible with a provider-mismatch diagnostic.

A successfully initialized context carries target key, data-store metadata needed by later workers, matched provider token, connection factory input, generation, physical-source fingerprint, lifecycle/latch observation, inventory/prerequisite results, and effective settings.

description: Implement the DocumentCache target registry/resolver with immutable snapshots and explicit refresh hooks. The initial membership set must come only from startup-bound DocumentCacheOptions. Refresh hooks must support startup, existing CMS refresh notifications, and later supervisor-triggered refresh without adding an independent hosted timer. For configured non-default tenant keys, refresh must call IDataStoreProvider.LoadDataStores(tenantKey) directly even when LoadTenants or loaded-tenant enumeration does not list the tenant. CMS auth, connectivity, timeout, invalid-response, and server errors must be operational target-resolution failures with retry diagnostics, not malformed local configuration.
acceptance-criteria: The registry exposes an immutable snapshot of every configured membership, current resolution state, current context generation, effective settings, and sanitized diagnostics.
Runtime membership does not expand from route qualifiers, JWT claims, recent requests, IDataStoreProvider.GetLoadedTenantKeys, LoadTenants, TenantExists, or the complete CMS inventory.
Configured targets missing from CMS remain Unresolved with retry diagnostics and are retried by explicit refresh hooks.
A configured non-default tenant refresh calls LoadDataStores(tenantKey) directly even if that tenant was not returned by LoadTenants and is not already loaded.

For an already resolved target, transient CMS refresh failure keeps the current target-context generation and attaches refresh-failure diagnostics until a successful refresh proves removal or replacement.
A successful refresh that no longer resolves the configured key reports Unresolved rather than creating a replacement generation.

A successful refresh whose only changes are route-context metadata, display metadata, tenant membership churn, or arbitrary DataStore fields that do not affect the matched provider token or connection factory input does not create a new target-context generation.

A successful refresh that changes the matched provider token or connection factory input, including the effective connection string, creates a new generation, resets process-local health evidence, rereads fingerprint/inventory/prerequisites, and does not change lifecycle or Kafka artifacts.

description: Expose target-scoped DocumentCache diagnostic snapshots for later 18-06 health composition. Diagnostics produced in this story are observations, not operational-health decisions. Include every configured target regardless of success or failure, and include enough detail for health/readiness to compose target status later while keeping messages sanitized and bounded.
acceptance-criteria: Diagnostics include target key, resolution state, provider token when known, target-context generation, opaque fingerprint when available, lifecycle state, cache-ahead latch state, inventory validation, enqueue-trigger validation, SQL Server prerequisite details, resolution retry state, effective settings, and sanitized failure category/message.
Diagnostics omit document bodies, connection strings, credentials, tenant display names, physical host names, database names, and raw source UUIDs.
A failed target does not hide peer target diagnostics or make the canonical relational API health surface fail by itself.

Diagnostics distinguish unresolved target, provider metadata missing, provider mismatch, connection string missing, inventory failure, provider prerequisite failure, unsupported prerequisite incident, and transient CMS refresh failure.
Unit tests cover successful and failed multi-target snapshots and sanitization of failure messages.

description: Define stable JSON-facing administrative request/result DTOs for guarded new-empty activation, offline read-acceleration activation, and offline deactivation. This story only defines the contracts and pure classifier inputs/outputs; it must not add an HTTP endpoint, CLI command runner, provider administrative mutex adapter, lock SQL, writer fence, cache/work clearing, baseline seeding, or state-mutating workflow. DTOs must use System.Text.Json, explicit property names, lower-camel enum strings, nested targetKey objects, and opaque fingerprint string serialization.
acceptance-criteria: Every JSON-facing request/result identifies the target as "targetKey": { "tenantKey": "", "dataStoreId": 1 }, with an empty string for the default tenant and a positive JSON number for dataStoreId.
Requests may include an expected physical-source fingerprint string that classifiers can compare against current target and downstream-publication observations.
JSON-facing enums serialize as explicit lower-camel strings such as tracking, internalOnly, providerPrerequisiteFailed, and unsupportedPrerequisiteIncident, and never as numeric enum values.
Result DTOs can report observed lifecycle, latch, fingerprint, target-context generation, rejection classification, sanitized diagnostics, and no-mutation guarantee details when available.

System.Text.Json tests pin property names, nested target-key shape, empty default-tenant serialization, dataStoreId numeric serialization, fingerprint serialization, lower-camel enum values, and rejection classification values.

description: Add the trusted downstream-publication-history abstraction and its default production implementation. The abstraction must return an observation rather than accepting a caller-supplied boolean or operator assertion. Until E19 supplies durable CDC binding state, the production default should return Unknown with sanitized diagnostics, while tests can use explicit fake observations. The observation must be bindable to the same normalized target key and current physical-source fingerprint used by offline activation/deactivation classifiers.
acceptance-criteria: The downstream-publication-history observation includes target key, observed physical-source fingerprint when available, status InternalOnly, Active, Historical, Possible, or Unknown, evidence source or generation identifier, observed time, and sanitized diagnostic text.
Offline activation/deactivation proof requires status InternalOnly for the same normalized target key and the same currently resolved physical-source fingerprint.
When the command request supplies an expected fingerprint, both the current target observation and downstream-publication-history observation must match that expected fingerprint.
The default production abstraction returns Unknown until E19 durable binding state is available.
Tests cover InternalOnly acceptance inputs and rejection inputs for Active, Historical, Possible, Unknown, missing fingerprint for resolved target, target mismatch, and fingerprint mismatch.

description: Implement pure lifecycle command preflight classifiers that consume 18-01 target observations plus command-time facts supplied later by 18-04 live preflight queries. Classifiers must produce the shared JSON-facing result classifications for guarded new-empty activation, offline activation, and offline deactivation without performing database mutation. Keep the split explicit: 18-04 owns administrative mutex acquisition, writer fencing, table locks, exclusive state-row locks, live nonempty checks, final rechecks, table clearing, baseline seeding, racing-insert handling, and session-loss behavior; 18-01 owns reusable result classification rules.
acceptance-criteria: Classifiers distinguish eligible, target not configured, target unresolved, target replaced before execution, missing or invalid inventory, provider prerequisite failed, unsupported prerequisite incident, lifecycle mismatch, Resetting requires explicit operator recovery, cache-ahead latch set, nonempty canonical/cache/work state for guarded new-empty activation, downstream history present or unknown, expected-source mismatch, and unexpected provider failure.
Every rejected result reports observed lifecycle, latch, fingerprint, target-context generation, and sanitized diagnostic details when available.
Every rejected result guarantees that no lifecycle, cache, work, latch, or provider-setting mutation was performed by the classifier.
Activation-preflight provider-prerequisite failure changes no lifecycle state, is retryable after correction, and is not satisfied by a previous startup validation.

Pure classifier tests cover legal and illegal transitions, Disabled/Rebuilding/Tracking/Resetting mismatches, target pause/resume by rollout, target replacement before execution, nonempty guarded activation rejection, cache-ahead latch rejection, provider-prerequisite rejection, unsupported-incident rejection, downstream binding rejection, and expected-source mismatch.
steps-to-verify: rg -n "pg_advisory_lock|sp_getapplock|TABLOCKX|LOCK TABLE|TRUNCATE|DELETE FROM .*DocumentCache|Disabled -> Tracking" src/dms | rg "DocumentCache|Projection"

description: Add focused cross-component acceptance coverage for DocumentCache target configuration and resolution that exercises realistic service registration, fake CMS responses, provider adapters, and multi-target isolation. This task fills gaps that are not naturally covered by the narrower unit tests in the implementation tasks, especially behavior across options, data-store metadata, target registry refresh, execution context initialization, diagnostics, and command classifiers.
acceptance-criteria: Integration-style tests prove malformed local DocumentCache options fail startup while CMS operational failures produce unresolved target diagnostics and do not fail unrelated targets.

Resolver tests cover unresolved configured targets, CMS refresh resolution, replacement context generation, no runtime membership hot reload, tenant-specific LoadDataStores calls for explicitly configured tenants, connection-string ineligibility, provider metadata missing/unknown, provider mismatch, target pause/resume by deployment rollout, and sanitized diagnostics.

Provider integration tests cover target prerequisite validation and isolation, initialization failure that remains ineligible for the lifetime of that execution context, successful validation by a newly initialized Disabled context after correction, and unsupported-incident classification for non-Disabled lifecycle observations.
Contract tests cover the stable JSON DTO shape and classifier result taxonomy used by 18-04 and later E19/bootstrap command surfaces.

The focused tests avoid implementing projector scheduling, cache-backed reads, health aggregation, CDC binding persistence, administrative mutex execution, or lifecycle mutation workflows assigned to other stories.
